artifacts.summary: Union-valued all three lean/core duplicated contract entries in agent-system/extensions/lean/index-entries.json, proved by an executed headless-Neovim merge reconstruction (pre-edit failure and post-edit success both demonstrated), and recorded the fresh 19-extension duplicated-path audit, the cslib ci-pipeline.md disposition, and two follow-up candidates without implementing either.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the lean mirror entry load-order defect by union-valuing load_when.agents on all three affected entries (contracts/adversarial-verification.md, contracts/reference-grounding.md, contracts/anti-analysis.md) in agent-system/extensions/lean/index-entries.json, proved via an executed core-then-lean merge reconstruction that fails pre-edit and passes post-edit. Re-ran the duplicated-path audit fresh across all 19 extensions, recorded the out-of-scope cslib internal-duplicate finding with explicit disposition, and recorded two follow-up candidates (a new check-extension-docs.sh lint rule and the content-level context/contracts override collision) without implementing either.

memory_candidates.content: When union-valuing a duplicated load_when.agents index entry across extensions (the merge.append_index_entries upsert-by-path defect class), re-run the cross-extension duplicate scan before assuming a path has only one other declaring extension. contracts/adversarial-verification.md turned out to be declared by THREE extensions (core, lean, cslib), not two -- a prior task had already union-valued cslib's copy using the identical pattern, so it showed up as 'already fixed' rather than a second instance of the live defect. A scoped scan (grep the two extensions named in the task) would have missed this; the full jq-based cross-extension scan over agent-system/extensions/*/index-entries.json caught it. Also useful: check-extension-docs.sh's rule-letter sequence currently ends at Rule U (EXTENSION.md length limit), so the next available letter for a new lint rule is Rule V.
